definition: Lexical simplification is a sub-task of text simplification.
details: It can be defined as any lexical substitution task that reduces text complexity.

explainer.lead: Lexical simplification is the text-simplification subtask of replacing words to reduce a text's complexity. It matters as one route to making text easier to read without rewriting its structure.

tiers.eli5: It is swapping hard words for easier ones — 'purchase' becomes 'buy' — while leaving the rest of the sentence alone.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers apply it as a substitution step within a text-simplification pipeline to lower reading difficulty. A pitfall is preserving meaning: a simpler word may not fit the original sense.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as any lexical substitution task that reduces text complexity, and as a sub-task of text simplification. The definition sets no threshold for how much complexity must fall.

explainer.example: In a simplified news article, 'commence' is replaced with 'start' to ease reading.
